Heliodorus, the Greek Ambassador to the court of the Shunga King Bhagabhadra erected the Heliodorus pillar near Vidisha.  Ujjain emerged as the predominant commercial centre of western India from the first century CE, located on the trade routes between the Ganges plain and India's Arabian Sea ports.  The Satavahana dynasty of the northern Deccan and the Saka dynasty of the Western Satraps fought for the control of Madhya Pradesh during the 1st to 3rd centuries CE.  The Satavahana King Gautamiputra Satakarni inflicted a crushing defeat upon the Saka rulers and conquered parts of Malwa and Gujarat in the 2nd century CE

Manipur.fact: ==== Vassal state of Konbaung dynasty ==== In the 18th century, Bodawpaya, the king of Burma acquired the Manipur (1814) along with the western kingdoms of Arakan (1784), Assam (1817).  By the medieval period, marriage alliances between the royal families of Manipur, Ahom kingdom and Burma had become common.  Medieval era manuscripts discovered in the 20th century, particularly the Puya, provide evidence that Hindus from the Indian subcontinent had married Manipur royalty by at least the 14th century.  In centuries thereafter, royal spouses came also from what is now Assam, Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh and from other South Indian kingdoms as well.  Another manuscript suggests that Muslims arrived in Manipur in the 17th century, from what is now Bangladesh, during the reign of Meidingu Khagemba.  The socio-political turmoil and wars, particularly the persistent and devastating Anglo-Burmese wars, affected the cultural and religious demography of Manipur.  === British colonial period === In 1824, the ruler of Manipur entered into a subsidiary alliance with the British Empire in the Indian subcontinent, which became responsible for Manipur's external defence

Manipur.subject: Indian States
Manipur.question: Yet the _____ in this battle was a turning point against the Japanese in East Asia
Manipur.fact: During World War II, Manipur was the scene of many fierce battles between Japanese invaders and British Indian forces.  The Japanese were beaten back before they could enter Imphal, which was one of the turning points of the overall war in South Asia.  The Battle of Imphal, known to the Manipuris as Japan Laan, are among the lesser-known battles of the Second World War.  Yet the Allied Victory in this battle was a turning point against the Japanese in East Asia.  === Post-colonial history === After the war, the Maharaja took the advice of the British Cabinet Mission and the Chamber of Princes to introduce democratic reforms in the state.  The Manipur State Constitution Act of 1947 was promulgated in July 1947 to give the state an elected legislative assembly and an appointed prime minister.  Elections to the assembly were held only in the following year

Manipur.subject: Indian States

Manipur.fact: Eventually Manipur was turned into a centrally administered province (called a 'Part C' state, later renamed union territory) by asking the Maharaja to sign a merger agreement.  He is believed to have signed it under duress.  Later, on 21 September 1949, he signed a Merger Agreement, disputed as having been done without consultation of the popular ministry under Manipur State Constitution Act 1947 and denial of the king's request to return to Manipur to discuss the same with his people.  Under 'duress' and 'coercion' Bodhachandra Singh signed the merger agreement merging the kingdom into India, which led to its becoming a Part C State.  The legislative assembly was dissolved and a centrally appointed Chief Commissioner handled the state's administration, as per the Constitution of India.  An advisory council with nominated members was provided to advise the Chief Commissioner.  In 1956, the advisory council was replaced by a territorial council with mostly elected members

Meghalaya.fact: The Khasi and Jaintia tribesmen follow the traditional matrilineal norm, wherein the Khun Khatduh (or the youngest daughter) inherits all the property and responsibilities for the family.  The male line, particularly the mother's brother, may indirectly control the ancestral property since he may be involved in important decisions relating to property including its sale and disposal.  In case a family has no daughters, the Khasi and Jaintia (also called Syntengs) have the custom of ia rap iing, where the family adopts a girl from another family, perform religious ceremonies with the community, and she then becomes ka trai iing (head of the house).  In the Garo lineage system, the youngest daughter inherits the family property by default, unless another daughter is so named by the parents.  She then becomes designated as nokna meaning 'for the house or home'.  If there are no daughters, a chosen daughter-in-law (bohari) or an adopted child (deragata) comes to stay in the house and inherit the property.  This adopted girl child is then the head of the house

Minkhaung I.question: Minkhaung I of Ava (Burmese: ပထမ မင်းခေါင် [pətʰəma̰ mɪ́ɰ̃ɡàʊɰ̃]; also spelled Mingaung; _____–1421) was king of Ava from 1400 to 1421
Minkhaung I.fact: Minkhaung I of Ava (Burmese: ပထမ မင်းခေါင် [pətʰəma̰ mɪ́ɰ̃ɡàʊɰ̃]; also spelled Mingaung; 1373–1421) was king of Ava from 1400 to 1421.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He is best remembered in Burmese history for his epic struggles against King Razadarit of Hanthawaddy Pegu in the Forty Years' War (_____–1424)
Minkhaung I.fact: He is best remembered in Burmese history for his epic struggles against King Razadarit of Hanthawaddy Pegu in the Forty Years' War (1385–1424).

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: As king, Minkhaung continued his father _____'s policy to restore the Pagan Empire
Minkhaung I.fact: As king, Minkhaung continued his father Swa Saw Ke's policy to restore the Pagan Empire. His father King Swa Saw Ke of Ava had met his commoner mother Saw Beza earlier in the year during a military campaign against Mohnyin.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Under the military leadership of his eldest son _____, Ava nearly succeeded
Minkhaung I.fact: Under the military leadership of his eldest son Minye Kyawswa, Ava nearly succeeded.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: While he ultimately failed to conquer Hanthawaddy and _____, he was able to bring in most of cis-Salween Shan states to the Ava orbit
Minkhaung I.fact: While he ultimately failed to conquer Hanthawaddy and Launggyet Arakan, he was able to bring in most of cis-Salween Shan states to the Ava orbit.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: His father _____ of Ava had met his commoner mother Saw Beza earlier in the year during a military campaign against Mohnyin
Minkhaung I.fact: His father King Swa Saw Ke of Ava had met his commoner mother Saw Beza earlier in the year during a military campaign against Mohnyin.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Chronicles say that after giving birth to the child, _____ showed up at the Ava palace to present the male son, as instructed to by the king
Minkhaung I.fact: His father King Swa Saw Ke of Ava had met his commoner mother Saw Beza earlier in the year during a military campaign against Mohnyin. Chronicles say that after giving birth to the child, Beza showed up at the Ava palace to present the male son, as instructed to by the king.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The child was named _____ (မင်းဆွေ [mɪ́ɴ sʰwè])
Minkhaung I.fact: The child was named Min Swe (မင်းဆွေ [mɪ́ɴ sʰwè]). Min Swe grew up in Ava (Inwa) until he was eight.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The king made Beza a junior queen, and had two more children with her: Theiddat and _____
Minkhaung I.fact: The king made Beza a junior queen, and had two more children with her: Theiddat and Thupaba Dewi.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Min Swe grew up in Ava (_____) until he was eight
Minkhaung I.fact: Min Swe grew up in Ava (Inwa) until he was eight.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Their older half-brother _____, who was born to a senior queen, constantly bullied both Swe and Theiddat
Minkhaung I.fact: Their older half-brother Tarabya, who was born to a senior queen, constantly bullied both Swe and Theiddat. The king kept Swe out of Tarabya's reach, and appointed his 11-year-old son governor of Pyinzi, a small town about 85 km southwest of Ava.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The king kept Swe out of _____'s reach, and appointed his 11-year-old son governor of Pyinzi, a small town about 85 km southwest of Ava
Minkhaung I.fact: Their older half-brother Tarabya, who was born to a senior queen, constantly bullied both Swe and Theiddat. The king kept Swe out of Tarabya's reach, and appointed his 11-year-old son governor of Pyinzi, a small town about 85 km southwest of Ava.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The bullying became a serious problem, and in _____/82, the king had to send away Swe and Theiddat to a small monastery near Pinle to study under the chief primate (Thinga-Yaza)
Minkhaung I.fact: The bullying became a serious problem, and in 1381/82, the king had to send away Swe and Theiddat to a small monastery near Pinle to study under the chief primate (Thinga-Yaza).

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The two princes studied under the learned monk, and traveled around the region, including _____, Minbu, Ngape and Padein, with their attendants
Minkhaung I.fact: The two princes studied under the learned monk, and traveled around the region, including Taungdwingyi, Minbu, Ngape and Padein, with their attendants.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He also gave Swe command of the 33-member _____ cavalry
Minkhaung I.fact: The king kept Swe out of Tarabya's reach, and appointed his 11-year-old son governor of Pyinzi, a small town about 85 km southwest of Ava. He also gave Swe command of the 33-member Pyinzi cavalry.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Swe would rule _____ for the next 15 years
Minkhaung I.fact: The king kept Swe out of Tarabya's reach, and appointed his 11-year-old son governor of Pyinzi, a small town about 85 km southwest of Ava. He also gave Swe command of the 33-member Pyinzi cavalry.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Chronicles have little information about Swe's period as governor except that his rivalry with _____ continued, and that the rivalry may have cost Ava's best chance of defeating Hanthawaddy Pegu
Minkhaung I.fact: The king kept Swe out of Tarabya's reach, and appointed his 11-year-old son governor of Pyinzi, a small town about 85 km southwest of Ava. Chronicles have little information about Swe's period as governor except that his rivalry with Tarabya continued, and that the rivalry may have cost Ava's best chance of defeating Hanthawaddy Pegu.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: In _____, the king ordered his two eldest sons to lead a two-pronged invasion of the southern kingdom in what would become known as the Forty Years' War
Minkhaung I.fact: In 1385, the king ordered his two eldest sons to lead a two-pronged invasion of the southern kingdom in what would become called the Forty Years' War.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Tarabya commanded the _____ (7000 infantry, 500 cavalry, 20 elephants) while Swe led the Second Army (6000 infantry, 500 cavalry, 20 elephants)
Minkhaung I.fact: Tarabya commanded the First Army (7000 infantry, 500 cavalry, 20 elephants) while Swe led the Second Army (6000 infantry, 500 cavalry, 20 elephants).

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The two princes were advised by Ava's best commanders, including Thilawa of Yamethin and _____
Minkhaung I.fact: The two princes were advised by Ava's best commanders, including Thilawa of Yamethin and Theinkhathu Saw Hnaung.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Tarabya, the overall commander-in-chief, sent a messenger, ordering Swe to hold his position and not to engage _____ until his army could reach the scene
Minkhaung I.fact: Tarabya's army pounced, driving back and pursuing Razadarit's army. Tarabya, the overall commander-in-chief, sent a messenger, ordering Swe to hold his position and not to engage Razadarit until his army could reach the scene.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Swe was assigned to guard the capital while Swa and _____ invaded the southern country again
Minkhaung I.fact: Swe was assigned to guard the capital while Swa and Tarabya invaded the southern country again.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Ava troops could not break through _____'s defenses and had to retreat before the rainy season arrived
Minkhaung I.fact: Ava troops could not break through Pegu's defenses and had to retreat before the rainy season arrived. At any rate, their army could not break through the Pegu defenses at Pankyaw although the campaign ended in a truce.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Swe was to get his chance again to go to the front in the _____–91 campaign
Minkhaung I.fact: Swe was to get his chance again to go to the front in the 1390–91 campaign.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: But this time, he commanded just a regiment, and was directly under the command of _____
Minkhaung I.fact: But this time, he commanded just a regiment, and was directly under the command of Tarabya.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: At any rate, their army could not break through the Pegu defenses at _____ although the campaign ended in a truce
Minkhaung I.fact: At any rate, their army could not break through the Pegu defenses at Pankyaw although the campaign ended in a truce.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The marriage was part of the effort by Ava and Mohnyin to mend their fences after the _____–88 war between the two states
Minkhaung I.fact: The marriage was part of the effort by Ava and Mohnyin to mend their fences after the 1387–88 war between the two states.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: On the advice of _____, King Swa selected Swe to marry Mi-Nauk
Minkhaung I.fact: On the advice of Chief Minister Min Yaza, King Swa selected Swe to marry Mi-Nauk.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: While the peace with _____ did not last—Ava and Mohnyin were to fight another war just three years later—the marriage between Swe and Mi-Nauk lasted
Minkhaung I.fact: The marriage was part of the effort by Ava and Mohnyin to mend their fences after the 1387–88 war between the two states. While the peace with Mohnyin did not last—Ava and Mohnyin were to fight another war just three years later—the marriage between Swe and Mi-Nauk lasted.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The couple had four children at Pyinzi: Minye Kyawswa, _____, Minye Thihathu and Minye Kyawhtin
Minkhaung I.fact: The couple had four children at Pyinzi: Minye Kyawswa, Saw Pyei Chantha, Minye Thihathu and Minye Kyawhtin.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Thihapate of _____ assassinated Tarabya, and tried to seize the throne
Minkhaung I.fact: Thihapate of Tagaung assassinated Tarabya, and tried to seize the throne.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: But the court executed the usurper, and offered the throne to _____
Minkhaung I.fact: But the court executed the usurper, and offered the throne to Min Swe.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Maha Pyauk of _____, who controlled a sizable army, and told the court to offer the throne to Pyauk instead
Minkhaung I.fact: Maha Pyauk of Yamethin, who controlled a sizable army, and told the court to offer the throne to Pyauk instead.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: When his brother still refused, _____ took matters into his own hand
Minkhaung I.fact: Theiddat implored Swe to reconsider. When his brother still refused, Theiddat took matters into his own hand.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Theiddat and his small band of men ambushed _____'s much bigger army near Ava while Pyauk was not expecting
Minkhaung I.fact: Maha Pyauk of Yamethin, who controlled a sizable army, and told the court to offer the throne to Pyauk instead. Theiddat and his small band of men ambushed Pyauk's much bigger army near Ava while Pyauk was not expecting.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Min Swe had been proclaimed king by 25 November _____ (or 26 October 1400)
Minkhaung I.fact: Min Swe had been proclaimed king by 25 November 1400 (or 26 October 1400).

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He assumed the title of Minkhaung (မင်းခေါင်; "_____" or "Paramount Lord")
Minkhaung I.fact: He assumed the title of Minkhaung (မင်းခေါင်; "Foremost Lord" or "Paramount Lord").

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He kept _____ as chief minister, and appointed Yaza's son Pauk Hla governor Yamethin, and Yaza's son-in-law Thado Theinkhathu governor of Badon and Tabayin
Minkhaung I.fact: He kept Min Yaza as chief minister, and appointed Yaza's son Pauk Hla governor Yamethin, and Yaza's son-in-law Thado Theinkhathu governor of Badon and Tabayin.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He also appointed _____ governor of Sagaing with the title of Thiri Zeya Thura but stopped short of declaring him his heir-apparent
Minkhaung I.fact: He also appointed Theiddat governor of Sagaing with the title of Thiri Zeya Thura but stopped short of declaring him his heir-apparent.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The Arakanese raided western _____ towns
Minkhaung I.fact: The Arakanese raided western Irrawaddy towns.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: In Pegu, _____ assessed that Minkhaung's hold on power was still weak, and planned to place a nominee of his own
Minkhaung I.fact: In Pegu, King Razadarit assessed that Minkhaung's hold on power was still weak, and planned to place a nominee of his own.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Throughout _____, Razadarit prepared an invasion river-borne fleet that could transport not only troops but even horses and elephants
Minkhaung I.fact: Throughout 1401, Razadarit prepared an invasion river-borne fleet that could transport not only troops but even horses and elephants.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: When the dry season began, _____ forces invaded by the Irrawaddy river, attacking all the riverside towns and cities, including their main targets, Prome (Pyay) and Ava (Inwa)
Minkhaung I.fact: When the dry season began, Hanthawaddy forces invaded by the Irrawaddy river, attacking all the riverside towns and cities, including their main targets, Prome (Pyay) and Ava (Inwa). Initially, Hanthawaddy held the advantage.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Initially, _____ held the advantage
Minkhaung I.fact: When the dry season began, Hanthawaddy forces invaded by the Irrawaddy river, attacking all the riverside towns and cities, including their main targets, Prome (Pyay) and Ava (Inwa). Initially, Hanthawaddy held the advantage.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States

Minkhaung I.fact: Ava did not have a navy that could challenge Pegu's massive flotilla. The Pegu navy held complete control of the Irrawaddy (as far north as Tagaung) but the blockades were not enough to force a surrender.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States

Minkhaung I.fact: Ava forces had to defend inside the fortified towns along the river: Prome, Myede, Sagu, Salin, Pakhan Nge, Salay, Pagan (Bagan), Talok, Pakhan Gyi, Sagaing and Ava.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The Pegu navy held complete control of the _____ (as far north as Tagaung) but the blockades were not enough to force a surrender
Minkhaung I.fact: The Pegu navy held complete control of the Irrawaddy (as far north as Tagaung) but the blockades were not enough to force a surrender.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States

Minkhaung I.fact: Minkhaung bought time by sending a delegation led by a learned Buddhist monk, Shin Zawtayanta, to broker a truce.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The monk delivered a sermon that _____ used as a pretense to withdraw from Ava
Minkhaung I.fact: The monk delivered a sermon that Razadarit used as a pretense to withdraw from Ava.

Minkhaung I.question: He was able to assemble a sizable force, which he sent after the rainy season to relieve _____
Minkhaung I.fact: He was able to assemble a sizable force, which he sent after the rainy season to relieve Prome. The Ava army decisively defeated the invaders south of Prome on 26 December 1402, forcing Pegu to ask for terms about ten days after the battle.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The Ava army decisively defeated the invaders south of Prome on 26 December _____, forcing Pegu to ask for terms about ten days after the battle
Minkhaung I.fact: The Ava army decisively defeated the invaders south of Prome on 26 December 1402, forcing Pegu to ask for terms about ten days after the battle.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States

Minkhaung I.fact: Minkhaung sent an embassy led by Min Yaza to Pegu to negotiate a treaty.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He wanted to exact a price from _____
Minkhaung I.fact: The Ava army decisively defeated the invaders south of Prome on 26 December 1402, forcing Pegu to ask for terms about ten days after the battle. Minkhaung sent an embassy led by Min Yaza to Pegu to negotiate a treaty.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The boundary of their kingdoms was fixed a little to the south of _____
Minkhaung I.fact: The boundary of their kingdoms was fixed a little to the south of Prome.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Pegu agreed to share the customs revenue of _____ (Pathein), and supply 30 elephants annually
Minkhaung I.fact: Pegu agreed to share the customs revenue of Bassein (Pathein), and supply 30 elephants annually.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: In return, Minkhaung sent his only sister _____ to be queen of Razadarit in a marriage alliance
Minkhaung I.fact: In return, Minkhaung sent his only sister Thupaba Dewi to be queen of Razadarit in a marriage alliance.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: In the following years, the king, with the advice of _____, resumed the expansionist policy of his father in order to restore the Pagan Empire

Minkhaung I.fact: His first targets were the nearer (cis-Salween) Shan states.

Minkhaung I.fact: According to the Burmese chronicles, the acquisition drive was largely peaceful, and accomplished through diplomatic missions led by Min Yaza to Onbaung (Hsipaw) in 1404/05, Nyaungshwe in 1405/06 and Mohnyin in 1406.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: According to the _____ chronicles, the attack on Myedu was carried out by another Shan state, Maw (Mong Mao/Mawdon Mawke)
Minkhaung I.fact: According to the Burmese chronicles, the acquisition drive was largely peaceful, and accomplished through diplomatic missions led by Min Yaza to Onbaung (Hsipaw) in 1404/05, Nyaungshwe in 1405/06 and Mohnyin in 1406.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: But the Ming records say that Ava's missions were in fact military expeditions, and that the Ming court became especially concerned after Ava's capture of Mohnyin in _____ that killed the sawbwa of Mo
Minkhaung I.fact: According to the Burmese chronicles, the acquisition drive was largely peaceful, and accomplished through diplomatic missions led by Min Yaza to Onbaung (Hsipaw) in 1404/05, Nyaungshwe in 1405/06 and Mohnyin in 1406. But the Ming records say that Ava's missions were in fact military expeditions, and that the Ming court became especially concerned after Ava's capture of Mohnyin in 1406 that killed the sawbwa of Mohnyin and his son.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: On 25 August _____, the Ming court sent an embassy to Ava to end the "aggression" against the Shan states
Minkhaung I.fact: According to the Burmese chronicles, the acquisition drive was largely peaceful, and accomplished through diplomatic missions led by Min Yaza to Onbaung (Hsipaw) in 1404/05, Nyaungshwe in 1405/06 and Mohnyin in 1406. But the Ming records say that Ava's missions were in fact military expeditions, and that the Ming court became especially concerned after Ava's capture of Mohnyin in 1406 that killed the sawbwa of Mohnyin and his son.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: It was not until _____ when he was about to resume the war with Pegu that he sent an embassy to Nanjing
Minkhaung I.fact: It was not until 1408 when he was about to resume the war with Pegu that he sent an embassy to Nanjing. Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: By September _____, the Ming court was considering a punitive action against Ava
Minkhaung I.fact: The Ming records say that the Ava representative offered a formal apology to the emperor for "having occupied" the Ming vassals "without authority" on 28 May 1408; but despite the promise, Ava was encouraging Hsenwi to rebel against the Ming in 1408–1409. By September 1409, the Ming court was considering a punitive action against Ava.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The simmering tensions would lead to war between Ava and Ming China between _____ and 1415
Minkhaung I.fact: The simmering tensions would lead to war between Ava and Ming China between 1412 and 1415.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The western kingdom was a tributary of Ava between _____/74 and 1385/86 during his father's reign but escaped Ava's orbit at the start of the Forty Years' War
Minkhaung I.fact: The western kingdom was a tributary of Ava between 1373/74 and 1385/86 during his father's reign but escaped Ava's orbit at the start of the Forty Years' War.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States

Minkhaung I.fact: Using alleged Arakanese raids on Ava's western districts, he sent a 10,000-strong army led by his eldest son Minye Kyawswa to Arakan. On 29 November 1406, Ava forces took the Arakanese capital Launggyet, and Min Saw Mon fled to Bengal.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Anawrahta of Kalay king of _____
Minkhaung I.fact: Using alleged Arakanese raids on Ava's western districts, he sent a 10,000-strong army led by his eldest son Minye Kyawswa to Arakan. On 29 November 1406, Ava forces took the Arakanese capital Launggyet, and Min Saw Mon fled to Bengal.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: On 29 November _____, Ava forces took the Arakanese capital Launggyet, and Min Saw Mon fled to Bengal
Minkhaung I.fact: On 29 November 1406, Ava forces took the Arakanese capital Launggyet, and Min Saw Mon fled to Bengal.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He tried to appease his brother _____, governor of Sagaing, by giving him command of the Northern Cavalry
Minkhaung I.fact: He tried to appease his brother Theiddat, governor of Sagaing, by giving him command of the Northern Cavalry. Theiddat felt totally betrayed.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: The king then appointed _____ his heir apparent, and married him to Saw Min Hla, a cousin of the groom
Minkhaung I.fact: The king then appointed Minye Kyawswa his heir apparent, and married him to Saw Min Hla, a cousin of the groom.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Minkhaung had _____ arrested but later released him after Min Yaza intervened
Minkhaung I.fact: Theiddat felt totally betrayed. Minkhaung had Theiddat arrested but later released him after Min Yaza intervened.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Shortly after, Theiddat fled to Pegu in _____
Minkhaung I.fact: Shortly after, Theiddat fled to Pegu in 1407.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: Realizing that Pegu was now Ava's only remaining target, _____ decided to act
Minkhaung I.fact: Realizing that Pegu was now Ava's only remaining target, Razadarit decided to act.

Minkhaung I.question: He readily gave shelter to _____ although he knew such an action would be regarded as a declaration of war against Ava
Minkhaung I.fact: Minkhaung had Theiddat arrested but later released him after Min Yaza intervened. Shortly after, Theiddat fled to Pegu in 1407.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He broke the _____ agreement: Pegu stopped sending the annual shipment of 30 elephants and Ava's share of customs revenue of the Bassein port
Minkhaung I.fact: He broke the 1403 agreement: Pegu stopped sending the annual shipment of 30 elephants and Ava's share of customs revenue of the Bassein port.

Minkhaung I.fact: Meanwhile, Minkhaung tried to solidify his hold over Arakan by sending his eldest daughter Saw Pyei Chantha to be the wife of Anawrahta as well as a senior minister to aid the vassal king.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States
Minkhaung I.question: He also sent an embassy to Chiang Mai, and a long overdue mission to China in early _____
Minkhaung I.fact: He also sent an embassy to Chiang Mai, and a long overdue mission to China in early 1408.

Minkhaung I.subject: Indian States

Mizoram.question: By the 18th century, various clans in the region united to form the Mizo identity, becoming the dominant inhabitants of the area, introducing the Mizo language, culture, and the _____ religion
Mizoram.fact: Early civilisations in Mizoram are believed to have thrived since around 600 BC, with significant archaeological evidence uncovered in the Vangchhia region.  Following this, Tibeto-Burman-speaking peoples gradually migrated from the Chin Hills in present-day Myanmar.  These groups formed organised chiefdoms and adopted jhum agricultural practices.  By the 18th century, various clans in the region united to form the Mizo identity, becoming the dominant inhabitants of the area, introducing the Mizo language, culture, and the Sakhua religion.  In the mid-19th century, the British conducted a series of military expeditions to assert control over the region, Mizoram was annexed by the British in 1895 and incorporated into the Assam Province.  Under British rule, the introduction of administrative reforms and the spread of Christianity significantly impacted Mizo society. Later, the Mizo Union (MU) and United Mizo Freedom Organisation (UMFO) emerged as political rivals, with the UMFO losing support after Mizoram joined India.  The MU opposed chieftainship, while Superintendent Leonard Lamb Peters supported the chiefs, leading to a civil disobedience movement in 1948.  Protests intensified, with the Mizo Union demanding Peters' removal, resulting in mass arrests and crackdowns until Assam's government mediated and replaced Peters in 1949 with Satyen Barkataki.  Barkataki would be the first Indian superintendent of the district and would establish the Aizawl-Lungleh road via voluntary labour, which would be widely covered in Indian newspapers. Nagaland.fact: Nagaland () is a state in the north-eastern region of India.  It is bordered by the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh to the north, Assam to the west, Manipur to the south, and the Naga Self-Administered Zone of the Sagaing Region of Myanmar (Burma) to the east.  Its capital city is Kohima and its largest city is the twin Chümoukedima–Dimapur.  The state has an area of 16,579 square kilometres (6,401 sq mi) with a population of 1,980,602 as per the 2011 Census of India, making it one of the least populated states in India.  Nagaland consists of 17 administrative districts, inhabited by 17 major tribes along with other sub-tribes.  Each tribe is distinct in character from the other in terms of customs, language and dress
